findings.description: Surplus withdrawal for one client burns shares from a communal pool, reducing totalBalanceOf() for all other clients. The proportional accounting model in totalBalanceOf() (line 132) distributes vault value by principal ratio, so burning shares for one client's surplus drains proportional yield from every other client.
findings.attackVector: SurplusWithdrawer.withdrawSurplusPercent() -> AYieldStrategy.withdrawFrom() -> _withdrawFrom() burns shared vault shares, reducing vault value visible to all clients via totalBalanceOf()

findings.description: _totalWithdraw ignores the cached `amount` parameter from the two-phase timelock system and reads live clientBalances instead. Deposits made during the 24-hour waiting period between Phase 1 and Phase 2 will be silently included in the withdrawal, undermining the timelock's community protection guarantee.
findings.codeSnippet:
uint256 clientStoredBalance = clientBalances[token][client];
uint256 sharesToWithdraw = (totalShares * clientStoredBalance) / totalDeposited[token];
findings.attackVector: Owner initiates totalWithdrawal (Phase 1 caches balance X). During 24h wait, additional deposits increase clientBalances to X+Y. Phase 2 execution withdraws X+Y, not the announced X.

findings.description: Fee-charging ERC4626 vaults cause totalBalanceOf() to overstate later depositors' balances. Principal tracking uses pre-fee amounts while share prices reflect post-fee values, creating phantom surplus that when extracted drains other clients' shares.
findings.attackVector: With fee-charging vault and multiple clients, SurplusWithdrawer extracts phantom surplus for later depositors, burning shares that proportionally belong to earlier depositors.

findings.description: When balanceHolder has zero principal but amount > 0, the principal cap reduces amount to 0, causing vault.redeem(0, ...) which reverts on many ERC4626 implementations. Missing early return after capping.
findings.attackVector: Authorized client calls withdraw(token, amount, recipientWithNoBalance). Transaction reverts unexpectedly at the vault level instead of handling gracefully.

findings.description: Base contract checks this.balanceOf() (returns principal) >= withdrawal amount, but withdrawFrom is designed for surplus extraction. When accumulated yield exceeds principal (>100% yield), the base check blocks legitimate surplus withdrawal. The deprecated balanceOf() is used for access control despite being marked DEPRECATED.
findings.codeSnippet:
uint256 clientBalance = this.balanceOf(token, client);
require(clientBalance >= amount, "AYieldStrategy: insufficient client balance");
findings.attackVector: Client deposits 100, vault generates 150 yield. SurplusWithdrawer tries to extract 150 surplus. Base contract checks: principalOf(client)=100 >= 150 = FALSE. Reverts, locking surplus.
